'''Nina Marković''' (born around 1970) is a Croatian-American physicist. Her work focuses on quantum transport in low-dimensional systems, superconductivity, nanostructures, and quantum computing. She received a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 2004. Marković worked at [[Delft University of Technology]], [[Harvard University]], and [[Johns Hopkins University]] before joining the [[Goucher College]] Department of Physics and Astronomy in 2015.

== Education ==
In 1993, Marković earned a Bachelor of Science in Physics from the [[University of Zagreb]] under advisor [[Boran Leontić]]. At [[University of Minnesota]] in 1998, she earned a doctorate in physics.<ref name=CV>{{Cite web|url=http://krieger.jhu.edu/physics/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/2013/02/January2015NinaMarkovicCV.pdf|title=Nina Markovic (CV)|last= Marković |first=Nina|date=2015|website=[[Johns Hopkins University]]|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref> She completed her thesis titled ''Transport properties and quantum phase transitions in ultrathin films of metals'' under her doctoral advisor [[Allen Goldman]] and received the [[Aneesur Rahman Award]] for best thesis.<ref name=thesis>{{cite thesis |last= Markovic |first=Nina |date=September 1998 |title=Transport properties and quantum phase transitions in ultrathin films of metals |type=Ph. D. |publisher=University of Minnesota |docket=9903638 |id={{ProQuest|304437608}} }}</ref> From 1998 to 2000, Marković conducted postdoctoral research at [[Delft University of Technology]] with [[Herre van der Zant]] and [[Hans Mooij]] ([[:de:Hans Mooij|de]]). She was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Harvard University]] where she conducted research with [[Michael Tinkham]] from 2000 to 2002.<ref name=CV/>

== Career ==
Marković joined the faculty at [[Johns Hopkins University]] as an assistant professor of physics and astronomy in 2003. She was awarded a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] by the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] in 2004.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://pages.jh.edu/~gazette/2006/13feb06/13nsf.html|title=Physicist Nina Markovic wins prestigious NSF CAREER Award|last=De Nike|first=Lisa|date=2006-02-13|website=Johns Hopkins Gazette|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref> In August 2004, she was awarded $99,999 from the [[National Science Foundation]] to conduct a study on quantum entanglement of electrons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0403964|title=NER: Superconductor-nanotube Entangler|date=2004|website=[[National Science Foundation]]|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref> She won a $500,000 [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation's Early CAREER Development Award]] to pursue research on electrical properties in nanometer scale materials in 2006.<ref name=":2" /> Marković was promoted to associate professor at Johns Hopkins in 2009.<ref name=CV /> In August 2011, she was awarded $360,000 from [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] to conduct a study on ''Spin Control in One-Dimensional Quantum Dots''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1106167|title=Spin Control in One-Dimensional Quantum Dots|date=2011|website=[[National Science Foundation]]|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref> In the fall of 2015, Marković joined the [[Goucher College]] Department of Physics and Astronomy as an associate professor in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.goucher.edu/intheloop/8115/new-faculty-for-fall-2015/|title=New Faculty for Fall 2015|date=2015-05-12|website=In The Loop|language=en|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://phys.org/news/2017-06-method-enable-stable-scalable-quantum.html|title=New method could enable more stable and scalable quantum computing, physicists report|last=Sundermier|first=Ali|date=2017-06-29|work=Phys.org|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref> In August 2015, she was awarded $430,371 from [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] to conduct a study on  ''Designing Quantum Matter with Superconducting Nanowires''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1663683&HistoricalAwards=false|title=Designing Quantum Matter with Superconducting Nanowires|date=2015|website=[[National Science Foundation]]|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref>

She is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and a member of the [[Materials Research Society]].<ref name=CV />
